Elastic-Net Random Generation

Source: R/enet_distrib.R
distrib_rng.EnetDistrib.Rd

Draws by the inverse transform, distrib_quantile(distrib, runif(n), theta). The quantile function of this family is closed form, so the transform is exact and costs one uniform per draw; the base class's ratio-of-uniforms fallback is not needed.

Arguments

distrib

An EnetDistrib object, from enet_distrib().

n

A single positive integer, the number of draws.

theta

A named list with components mu, lambda and alpha, each a numeric vector of length 1 or of length n; a component of length 1 is recycled.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A numeric vector of n draws, symmetric about mu.

See also

distrib_quantile.EnetDistrib(), which it inverts through, variance.EnetDistrib() for the moment the draws reproduce, and distrib_rng() for the generic.

Examples

d <- enet_distrib()
th <- list(mu = 0, lambda = 2, alpha = 0.5)

set.seed(71)
x <- distrib_rng(d, 2e5, th)

# Two moments against their closed forms, and the symmetry.
rbind(sample = c(mean(x), var(x), mean((x - mean(x))^3) / sd(x)^3),
      theory = c(mean(d, th), variance(d, th), skewness(d, th)))
#>                 [,1]      [,2]         [,3]
#> sample -0.0005352337 0.4778600 -0.008027417
#> theory  0.0000000000 0.4748647  0.000000000

# As alpha approaches one the draws become Laplace.
set.seed(72)
xl <- distrib_rng(d, 1e5, list(mu = 0, lambda = 2, alpha = 1 - 1e-10))
c(sample_var = var(xl), laplace_var = 2 / 2^2)
#>  sample_var laplace_var 
#>   0.4889258   0.5000000
